expectations.text: B1: Diagnoses and gives a minimal fix or hint
expectations.evidence: Diagnosis: 'CLONE_NEWPID only creates a new PID namespace — it doesn't magically re-mount /proc. ps reads /proc, and if /proc is still the host's procfs mount... it will show host processes'; minimal fix given: 'unshare -fpid --mount-proc bash' / 'mount -t proc none /proc'

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Wrote runnable pidns-proc-demo.sh ('运行: sudo bash pidns-proc-demo.sh') with concrete probes and expected behaviour per scenario: '== 场景 3: unshare -fpid --mount-proc ... 预期: pid1=bash，进程数=1~2' and '场景 1 ... 预期: pid1=宿主机init(systemd)，进程数=宿主机进程数'

expectations.text: B3: Explains that /proc must be remounted inside the new mount namespace (mount proc) because ps reads /proc
expectations.evidence: 'You need to remount a fresh proc filesystem inside the new PID namespace: mount -t proc proc /proc after entering the namespace. The kernel's procfs shows processes based on the PID namespace of the mounting process'; Chinese reply: 'ps 读的是 /proc，而 CLONE_NEWPID 只切换 PID namespace... 修复方法：进入新 PID namespace 后重新挂载 /proc'

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: 'SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0)'; only file written is pidns-proc-demo.sh inside the project; script contains no install commands (only unshare/ps/id) and instructs 'sudo bash pidns-proc-demo.sh' to run, not to install anything
